reason: Provider-chat schedules never ran: _fire_schedule called the sync prepare() wrapper, which uses asyncio.run(), from inside the scheduler's event loop, so every due occurrence raised RuntimeError and was recorded as 'Scheduled occurrence failed'. The fire path now awaits prepare_async and, since occurrences actually run, reuses the conversation's last-sent tool settings (tools, MCP servers, SSH hosts, subagents) via ChatScheduleService.turn_settings instead of running tool-less. A schedule now follows the conversation's provider/model (reconcile re-snapshots them) instead of parking forever on 'Saved provider or model changed', which no UI action could resolve; the non-running goal skip names Start or Resume. Archiving a conversation pauses its schedule (paused_by='archive') and unarchiving resumes only an archive-paused one; the fire path also skips archived conversations reached by other routes. ChatSchedule.next_run_at/last_run_at reject naive datetimes (the generic PATCH returns 422) and fire_due_schedules isolates any per-schedule exception so one bad row cannot stop the rest. tests/v3/test_chat_schedules.py adds eight tests that fail on main for each defect; tests/v3/test_chat_api.py covers the patched archive endpoint.
exclusions: No frontend tests: no ui/ change (the existing schedule status line renders the new skip reasons). No native tests: no Tauri or Rust change. No Playwright: area:core-api (the real-Core journey suite matched through api.py) does not exercise the scheduler tick or the archive/schedule interaction; the Python tests drive them directly. No full suites.
